prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

You are reviewing layouts of one table, all rendered in a real browser with identical content, font, padding and colours; only column widths differ. You do not know who or what produced them. The first image is the content overview (every cell on one line).
Table: RTL · صفوف معنونة (language ar, right-to-left: column 1 is on the RIGHT).
Grid: 4 columns × 4 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 13px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "البند" · longest unbreakable word 58px · one-line width 151px
  col 2: header "الربع الأول" · longest unbreakable word 26px · one-line width 54px
  col 3: header "الربع الثاني" · longest unbreakable word 30px · one-line width 58px
  col 4: header "ملاحظات" · longest unbreakable word 52px · one-line width 384px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 453px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 452px.
Fixed: content, font, 13px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Rate EACH layout independently: "excellent" | "good" | "acceptable" | "poor" | "bad", with a short reason that points at what you see. Then name the best layout(s) (ties allowed), say how confident you are (low/medium/high), and note anything you are unsure about.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"ratings":{"A":{"grade":"","why":""},"B":{"grade":"","why":""},"C":{"grade":"","why":""},"D":{"grade":"","why":""},"E":{"grade":"","why":""},"F":{"grade":"","why":""}},"best":["letter"],"confidence":"","unsure":""}

log.raw: {"ratings":{"A":{"grade":"poor","why":"The two quarter columns have ample empty space, while the notes wrap into many short lines and the first row label also wraps."},"B":{"grade":"acceptable","why":"The quarter headers fit and the row labels are readable, but the wide row-header column leaves the first note in four lines."},"C":{"grade":"acceptable","why":"The notes read comfortably in two lines, but both quarter headers wrap and make the paired numeric columns feel cramped."},"D":{"grade":"excellent","why":"Both quarter headers fit on one line, the row labels remain readable, and the notes have enough width for a balanced three-line first row."},"E":{"grade":"poor","why":"The row-header column is wide enough for every label on one line, but the first note is squeezed into five short lines."},"F":{"grade":"excellent","why":"The paired quarter columns have clear one-line headers, while the notes and row labels wrap comfortably and preserve a compact row rhythm."}},"best":["D","F"],"confidence":"high","unsure":"D and F are very close; their small differences in width do not produce a clear visual winner."}
